training_source: Qwen-7B and Whisper-large-v3 initialization; report states evaluation-data exclusion, but full backbone and pre/post-training corpus provenance is unavailable
notes: Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct gets one conversation per clip in its chat template: the system prompt, then one user turn with the audio first and the user prompt after it (as in the model card), with the system and user prompts of `scripts/llm_eval/prompts.yaml` (the same as for GPT Realtime); the clip as 16 kHz mono (at most its first 30 s)

Greedy decoding (do_sample=False, no repetition penalty), at most 24 new tokens, bfloat16 on `mps`, sdpa attention; so the answers are the same from run to run (up to rounding differences between devices)

The answer is read by `scripts/llm_eval/parsing.py` and becomes a one-hot vector over the 7 configured emotions plus `invalid`. Allowed answers for this run: angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, sad, surprised. An answer that is not exactly one allowed label gets a follow-up in the same conversation ("Answer with exactly one word from this list, in lowercase, and nothing else: angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, sad, surprised."), up to 1 time(s); then `invalid`
An answer that is not one of the dataset's emotions counts as wrong (column *other answer* of the confusion matrices); the raw answers are in `outputs/qwen2_audio_7b/responses.jsonl`

columns.audio_path: audio file, relative to the emotion_recognition/ folder
columns.acted_emotion: ground truth: the emotion each actress was asked to portray, from the last word of the file name (`angry`, `disgust`, `fear`, `happy`, `neutral`, `ps` for pleasant surprise, `sad`)
columns.prediction: model prediction: the most probable of the 7 emotions evaluated (angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, surprised, sad)
columns.prediction_all_classes: model prediction: the most probable of all 8 model classes
columns.p_*: model probability of each of its 8 classes (they add up to 1)
columns.token_p_*: audio LLMs: the model's probability of each label at the first generated position (first-token probabilities, renormalised over the labels; they add up to 1); the prediction is still the parsed answer
columns.token_mass: audio LLMs: the share of the whole vocabulary that the labels' first tokens get at that position
